SLUGS: axislabel-formatter-index, then axislabel-formatter-indexing

1) axislabel-formatter-index — feat(axis): axisLabel `formatter` can receive its index for working with `customValues`. Context: Axis label callbacks can format the label value, but authors working with `customValues` also need to know which generated tick they are formatting. Desired: `axisLabel.formatter` receives the tick index as an additional argument so formatter logic works reliably with `customValues`. Acceptance: a formatter declared as `axisLabel.formatter(value, index)` receives the expected index for each displayed custom tick. Likely files: src/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.ts, src/component/axis/AxisBuilder.ts, src/coord/axisCommonTypes.ts (formatter type signatures).

2) axislabel-formatter-indexing — fix(axis): refactor axisLabel formatter. Context: with axisLabel.customValues, when some custom values are filtered out because they fall outside the visible axis extent, the formatter callback can receive the wrong index for repeated/duplicate values, because the label-building path looks the position back up from the filtered tick list (e.g. indexOf) instead of preserving the mapped position directly. Desired: when building labels from `axisLabel.customValues`, the formatter is called with the actual index of each rendered item in the filtered label sequence, including duplicate numeric values; duplicated values must not collapse onto the first matching position. Everything else about axis label rendering, formatter signatures, and label text generation stays unchanged. Likely file: src/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.ts (and possibly the AxisBuilder call site). IMPORTANT: do not touch src/scale/* or src/util/number.ts — another agent owns those.

SLUG: axis-min-max-nullable — fix(type): add missing nullable type for the axis `min` and `max` option. TypeScript users can return `null` or `undefined` from axis `min`/`max` callbacks at runtime (documented pattern: returning null/undefined means auto), but the type declarations reject it. Make the type surface for axis min/max allow nullable callback results (the callback form may return the value or null/undefined). No runtime change. Likely file: src/coord/axisCommonTypes.ts. Verify with `npx tsc --noEmit` and, if practical, a small type test. Do not touch src/scale/* or src/util/number.ts.

SLUG: candlestick-series-encode-render — fix(candlestick): fix candlestick render error with `series.encode`. Candlestick charts render incorrectly or crash when data is mapped through `series.encode`, particularly in non-default layouts (e.g. horizontal/transposed or swapped open/close/low/high dimension mapping). Candlestick rendering must honor series.encode across supported layouts: correct orientation and geometry of candle bodies and whiskers. Likely files: src/chart/candlestick/CandlestickView.ts, src/chart/candlestick/CandlestickSeries.ts, src/chart/candlestick/candlestickLayout.ts.

SLUGS: time-axis-customvalues-formatter, then cartesian-small-number-rounding, then logscale-negative-exponent-rounding

1) time-axis-customvalues-formatter — fix(axis): fix chart does not work when using `customValues` with `formatter` in time axis label. A time axis combining axisLabel.customValues with a custom axisLabel.formatter breaks (crash or dropped axis); it must render normally and pass the formatter the expected label values. Likely in the axis label building path (src/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.ts) and/or src/scale/Time.ts. Note: another agent is concurrently editing src/component/axis/AxisBuilder.ts and src/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.ts for a related formatter-index feature — coordinate by keeping your changes to those files minimal and additive; you own src/scale/* and src/util/number.ts exclusively.

2) cartesian-small-number-rounding — Fix that extreme small numbers can not be displayed in Cartesian due to inappropriate rounding precision. Axis extent and tick calculation must preserve enough precision for extremely small numbers across interval, time, and log scale handling so those data points remain visible (e.g. data around 1e-15). Likely files: src/util/number.ts (round/getPrecisionSafe), src/scale/Interval.ts, src/scale/Time.ts, src/scale/Log.ts, src/scale/helper.ts.

3) logscale-negative-exponent-rounding — fix(logScale): incorrect rounding usage; support data with big negative exponent. Log-scale charts with very large negative exponents (tiny magnitudes like 1e-30) hit incorrect rounding paths causing unstable ticks. Log-scale rounding must handle extremely small values consistently. Likely files: src/scale/Log.ts, src/util/number.ts. Verify with focused unit tests (test/ut has scale specs — look for existing log/number specs and extend or add your own under /workspace/agent_tests/).

SLUG: bar-zero-size-labels — fix(bar): fix wrong label position when bar width/height is 0. Bar labels can end up on the wrong side when a bar's width or height is zero (sparse/collapsed datasets). Zero-size bars must still place outside labels according to the intended axis direction and inversion rules instead of falling back to a misleading default side. Investigate the bar label position computation (likely src/chart/bar/BaseBarSeries.ts and/or src/label/labelLayoutHelper.ts-related helpers used by bar). Keep changes minimal; do not refactor pie label layout (another agent owns src/chart/pie and src/label/labelLayoutHelper.ts — if the fix truly belongs there, keep it tightly scoped and additive).

SLUGS: chord-export-entry, then typescript-export-types

1) chord-export-entry — fix(chord): add missing export entry for chord chart. The packaged library is missing the expected export entry for the chord chart even though the implementation exists (look at src/chart/chord/ and how other charts are exposed, e.g. src/export/charts.ts, and any charts.d.ts / index files that enumerate chart entries). The published package should expose the chord chart so consumers can `import { ChordChart } from 'echarts/charts'` and register it normally.

2) typescript-export-types — fix(type): fix missing or mismatched TS export types. TypeScript consumers hit missing or mismatched exported option types, especially for series that combine shared coordinate-system mixins. The published TS surface should export the correct option types for affected series and include the calendar and matrix coordinate-system mixins where those series actually support them. Investigate src/export/option.ts (or wherever SeriesOption unions and per-series option exports are assembled) and compare each series' option interface against the coordinate systems the series supports at runtime. IMPORTANT: confine changes to src/export/** and pure type-declaration files; do not edit src/chart/* or src/component/* implementation files (other agents own those). Verify with `npx tsc --noEmit`.

SLUGS: datazoom-single-point-position, then slider-handlelabel-optional

1) datazoom-single-point-position — fix(dataZoom): fix wrong position of the dataZoom when the series has only one data point. With a single-point series the slider dataZoom computes invalid geometry (e.g. NaN/Infinity from a zero-length extent or division by zero) and renders in the wrong place. It must place itself correctly for one-point charts. Likely files: src/component/dataZoom/SliderZoomView.ts, src/component/dataZoom/* .

2) slider-handlelabel-optional — fix(type): `emphasis.handleLabel` of slider dataZoom should be an optional type. The type contract currently makes emphasis.handleLabel required although the runtime accepts its absence. Make it optional; runtime unchanged. Likely in src/component/dataZoom type definitions. Verify with `npx tsc --noEmit`.

SLUG: gauge-progress-auto-color — feat(gauge): `progress.color` supports 'auto'. Gauge progress arcs currently require manual color duplication; `progress.color: 'auto'` should make the progress fill follow the series color mapping automatically (similar to how other gauge visuals can inherit the series color). Likely files: src/chart/gauge/GaugeView.ts, src/chart/gauge/GaugeSeries.ts. Follow the real upstream implementation approach for how 'auto' resolves (e.g. via getVisual('color') or series color palette).

SLUG: graph-nodescaleratio-type — fix(type): fix `nodeScaleRatio` option type for graph series. The TS declaration for graph `nodeScaleRatio` is narrower than runtime behavior (declared as a single fixed literal such as `0.6` instead of `number`), so valid numeric configs look illegal. Widen the public type to accept numbers; runtime unchanged. Likely file: src/chart/graph/GraphSeries.ts. Verify with `npx tsc --noEmit`.

SLUG: jitter-overlap-avoidance — fix(jitter): fix overlap when there is enough space to avoid. Scatter jitter with overlap avoidance still leaves points overlapping even when free space exists within the allowed jitter band. When overlap avoidance is enabled, placement must consistently choose a non-overlapping position whenever a valid position exists inside the permitted movement range, falling back only when space is genuinely exhausted; adjusted points must stay within the jitter budget. Investigate the jitter implementation (search src/ for 'jitter', likely src/util/ or src/chart/scatter/ or src/chart/helper/). Study the existing algorithm (grid/placement based) and fix the placement logic. Verify with a focused unit test if feasible (there may be an existing jitter spec under test/ut).

SLUG: line-areastyle-empty-dimension — fix(line): fix areaStyle render error when dimension name is empty string. Line series with areaStyle throws a render error when a dataset uses an empty string ('') as a dimension name. Area rendering must tolerate empty-string dimension names instead of treating them as a fatal path. Likely files: src/chart/line/LineView.ts, src/chart/line/helper.ts, or the polygon/area draw helpers. Reproduce first with a small test case (line series + areaStyle + dataset with a dimension named ''), then fix minimally.

SLUG: lines-loop-symbol-flip — fix(lines): fix effect symbol flip on unidirectional loop end when `roundTrip` is not enabled. Animated effect symbols on one-way looping `lines` series briefly flip direction when crossing the loop endpoint. When roundTrip is not enabled, the effect symbol must preserve a consistent forward orientation across the loop boundary. Likely files: src/chart/helper/EffectSymbol.ts, src/chart/helper/LineDraw.ts, src/chart/lines/*. Look at how rotation/tangent is computed at the loop wrap-around point.

SLUG: marker-z-option — feat(marker): markPoint markLine markArea support z option. Marker overlays (markPoint/markLine/markArea) should accept a `z` option so authors can place marker overlays at the intended rendering depth, like other chart elements. Implement across the marker component: option type, model default handling, and view group z application. Likely files: src/component/marker/MarkerModel.ts, src/component/marker/MarkPointModel.ts/View, MarkLineModel/View, MarkAreaModel/View, markerHelper. Follow how `silent` and similar options flow through. Verify with `npx tsc --noEmit` and a focused render test if practical.

SLUG: parallel-axis-extent — fix(parallel): fix incorrect axis extent when any subsequent series has a larger value than the first. Parallel coordinates compute the axis extent from the first contributing series and fail to expand it for later series with larger values, clipping/mis-scaling valid data. Extent calculation must account for ALL contributing series before finalizing the range. Likely files: src/coord/parallel/ParallelModel? src/component/parallel/*, src/coord/parallel/AxisModel.ts, parallelPreprocessor. Reproduce with two series where the second has larger values, then fix.

SLUG: seriesdata-each-example — chore: fix example description for the `each` method of `SeriesData`. The examples for `SeriesData.each` and `DataStore.each` currently suggest only named dimensions are supported; the API also supports numeric dimension indexes. Update the doc-comment examples (src/data/SeriesData.ts, src/data/DataStore.ts) to demonstrate valid iteration usage including numeric dimension indexes. Runtime behavior unchanged — comments/docs only. Keep the existing doc style.

SLUG: sunburst-root-label-centering — fix(sunburst): fix root node label may not be centered. Sunburst root labels can drift off center in the full-circle root case due to floating-point angle math (e.g. start/end angle not exactly equal after computation). The root-node label must stay centered for a full-circle root. Likely file: src/chart/sunburst/SunburstView.ts or sunburstLayout.ts — look at how the root label angle/position is derived and add an appropriate epsilon/tolerance. Keep minimal.

SLUG: toolbox-emphasis-color — fix(toolbox): fix emphasis color to be different with default color. The toolbox hover/emphasis state is not visually distinct because the emphasis color can collapse to the default icon color. Toolbox emphasis styling should use a different highlight color so `emphasis.iconStyle.borderColor` produces a clearly different visual highlight. Likely files: src/component/toolbox/ToolboxModel.ts (default emphasis iconStyle) — check how the default iconStyle.borderColor is defined and how theme colors feed it. Do not edit src/theme/dark.ts (another agent owns it).

SLUG: tooltip-listener-unbinding — fix(tooltip): fix potential memory leakage by explicitly unbinding event listeners. Repeatedly creating/disposing tooltip-heavy charts accumulates leftover DOM listeners from the HTML tooltip. Disposing or rebuilding chart tooltips must fully release the HTML tooltip event wiring. Likely files: src/component/tooltip/TooltipHTMLContent.ts (and possibly TooltipView.ts) — look for DOM event listeners added (mousemove/click on the tooltip el or document) without matching removal in dispose, and add explicit unbinding. Add a regression test under /workspace/agent_tests/tooltip-listener-unbinding/ if practical.

SLUG: vue-raw-instance — fix(core): mark echarts instance object as raw in Vue. Vue users store chart instances in ref()/reactive(); proxying the ECharts instance breaks instance methods. An ECharts instance should be treated as raw by Vue reactivity. The standard upstream approach: define a non-enumerable (or Symbol-keyed) `__v_skip` property on the instance (Vue 3's markRaw flag) when the instance is created, in src/core/echarts.ts (ECharts class constructor), guarded so it has no effect outside Vue. Type it appropriately without adding a Vue dependency. Verify with `npx tsc --noEmit`.

SLUG: notice-year-2026 — chore: update NOTICE year to 2026. Update the shipped NOTICE file so it states `Copyright 2017-2026 The Apache Software Foundation`. Check the NOTICE file at /workspace/NOTICE (and any other copies of that copyright line used in distribution, e.g. in build/ templates or dist headers if present — but only where it's the NOTICE copyright line). No other content changes.

SLUG: prepublish-semicolon — fix: Fix missing semicolon in pre-publish.js. A syntax mistake (missing semicolon) in the publish script can derail the packaging workflow. Inspect build/pre-publish.js, find the missing semicolon / syntax error, fix it, and verify the script parses (e.g. `node --check build/pre-publish.js`; note the repo has "type": "module" so check module syntax appropriately). Minimal change.

SLUG: lint-changed-files-pattern — fix(workflow): fix match pattern for changed files collection in the lint action. The lint CI workflow misses changed TypeScript files placed directly under the source root because the diff glob pattern doesn't catch them (e.g. pattern like `src/**/*.ts` does not match `src/foo.ts` with certain glob engines, or an over-anchored pattern). Inspect .github/workflows/ci.yml (and any other workflow collecting changed files for linting), fix the pattern so files directly under the source root are included. Workflow YAML only, no product change.

SLUGS: label-layout-margin, then labelline-smooth-reset, then pie-tangential-noflip

You own src/chart/pie/** and src/label/labelLayoutHelper.ts.

1) label-layout-margin — Fix/label layout margin. Chart authors hit inconsistent label spacing/overlap behavior across pie charts and shared label layout code around margins, stroke-aware bounds, and post-layout updates. Label layout should apply the same geometry rules everywhere so `minMargin`, `textMargin`, hidden-overlap handling, and final label bounds behave consistently after layout adjustments; overlap prevention must reflect the final rendered label geometry. Study src/label/labelLayoutHelper.ts and pie label usage (src/chart/pie/labelLayout.ts) and align the margin math.

2) labelline-smooth-reset — fix(label): fix labelLine `smooth` can not be reset. Pie labels keep a stale curved guide line after labelLine.smooth is turned off or reset to 0. Changing smooth back to false/0 must fully reset the guide line to a straight path on option update (setOption merge/update path). Likely in src/chart/pie/PieView.ts or labelLayout.ts where the polyline points are computed — ensure the smooth branch is re-evaluated and old curvature isn't retained.

3) pie-tangential-noflip — feat(pie): add `tangential-noflip` rotation mode. Pie labels can follow the tangent of the slice via label.rotate 'tangential', but it may flip labels upside down. Add a `label.rotate` mode named `tangential-noflip` so tangential labels stay aligned to the slice without flipping to the opposite reading direction. Update the rotation computation in src/chart/pie/labelLayout.ts and the type for label.rotate (check src/util/types.ts or pie series option types).

SLUGS: radar-blur-itemstyle, then radar-style-precedence, then radar-clockwise-option. You own src/chart/radar/**.

1) radar-blur-itemstyle — fix(radar): itemStyle of blur not working. Radar blur-state styling is configured but `blur.itemStyle` never takes effect — blurred points keep normal appearance. Blur styling must honor the state-specific style contract: `blur.itemStyle` and related blur lineStyle/areaStyle must apply when the series is blurred. Study how RadarView applies states to symbols and the polygon/polyline (src/chart/radar/RadarView.ts, RadarSeries.ts state mixing).

2) radar-style-precedence — fix(radar): improve logic and add test cases of #21081. After the blur fix, state-specific radar styling can still be overridden in some interaction paths, so `emphasis.itemStyle` and blur styling don't always win. Ensure state transitions preserve intended precedence: emphasis/blur visuals are applied consistently instead of being overwritten by default symbol styling (look at how itemStyle is re-applied on state change, e.g. useStateOverride/itemStyle normal defaults clobbering emphasis). Add unit tests under /workspace/agent_tests/radar-style-precedence/ if practical.

3) radar-clockwise-option — feat(radar): add `clockwise` option. Radar coordinate systems should support a `clockwise` option controlling the direction in which indicators are laid out (default preserves current behavior). Update src/coord/radar/Radar.ts (angle computation), RadarModel (option + default), and keep label placement/rendering correct. Check how indicator angles are computed and multiply/flip as appropriate. Verify type check passes.

SLUGS: matrix-dimension-length, then matrix-label-api, then matrix-label-formatter. You own src/coord/matrix/** and src/component/matrix/**.

1) matrix-dimension-length — feat(matrix): support matrix.x/y.length for conveniently creating a headless matrix without composing an array. Currently creating a headless matrix requires explicit coordinate arrays; allow `matrix.x.length` and `matrix.y.length` to declare the size directly while existing array-based definitions keep working. Look at how matrix x/y coordinates are parsed (src/coord/matrix/Matrix.ts? MatrixModel) and extend option types.

2) matrix-label-api — Fix matrix label API. Matrix labels do not reliably inherit shared text defaults (they should inherit `option.textStyle` like other labels), and matrix coordinate lookup can return invalid locator ranges in edge cases — handle invalid locator ranges predictably, including the `coordClamp` path, when some locator values are missing or out of bounds. Likely files: src/component/matrix/MatrixView.ts (label creation), src/coord/matrix/* (locator/clamp logic).

3) matrix-label-formatter — fix(matrix): fix matrix label formatter does not work. Declared label formatters are not applied: matrix labels ignore both template strings and callback formatters. Matrix labels must honor `label.formatter` (string templates and functions), and formatter callbacks must receive the expected matrix label context such as `name`, `value`, and `coord`. Likely in src/component/matrix/MatrixView.ts label setup and any label params construction.

SLUGS: darkmode-lightness-algorithm, then visualmap-darkmode-inrange, then matrix-darkmode-colors, then toolbox-dataview-darkmode. You own src/theme/dark.ts.

1) darkmode-lightness-algorithm — fix(theme): adjust dark mode color lightness algorithm. The dark-mode token lightness adjustment does not create enough contrast between related colors, so charts look flat. Dark-theme color derivation must preserve stronger lightness contrast so derived colors remain distinguishable while staying in-palette. Look at src/theme/dark.ts for the lightness adjust/shift helper and tune the algorithm (e.g. multiplicative vs additive adjustment).

2) visualmap-darkmode-inrange — fix(visualMap): fix dark mode should not provide inRange. In dark mode, visualMap still injects default `inRange` colors which can override users' own mappings. The dark theme must stop supplying a default visualMap.inRange color mapping. In src/theme/dark.ts remove/adjust the visualMap inRange defaults (keeping other visualMap theme values intact as appropriate).

3) matrix-darkmode-colors — fix(matrix): fix darkMode color. Matrix charts in dark mode use colors tuned for light backgrounds; borders/dividers/structural surfaces become hard to distinguish. The dark theme should provide matrix-specific colors keeping the matrix body, dividers, and borders legible on dark backgrounds. Add/adjust matrix section colors in src/theme/dark.ts (check what option keys src/component/matrix reads).

4) toolbox-dataview-darkmode — fix(toolbox): fix dataView component does not fit dark mode. The toolbox dataView popup looks light-themed in dark mode. Dark mode must style the data view surface, text, textarea, and controls coherently. Look at src/component/toolbox/feature/DataView.ts (hardcoded background/color styles) and src/theme/dark.ts toolbox section; derive the popup colors from the theme (dark mode API: check how other components read theme/darkMode).

SLUG: visualmap-unbounded-range — VisualMap support unboundedRange. Continuous visual maps force both ends of `range` to be hard bounds. Add a `visualMap.unboundedRange`-style capability so users can mark one side of the selected interval as open-ended: with it enabled, a range touching the configured min or max behaves as an open interval on that side while the opposite bound remains effective. Implement in the continuous visualMap component (src/component/visualMap/ContinuousModel.ts, ContinuousView.ts) with option types and defaults; do not edit src/theme/dark.ts (another agent owns it). Verify `npx tsc --noEmit` and add a focused unit test if practical.
